# Digital Marketing Malaysia Price Guide 2026: RM888 to RM15,000 a Month

**Digital marketing price in Malaysia starts from around RM888 for an entry package and runs to RM15,000 a month for full-service work.** Most SME retainers land between RM1,500 and RM8,000: freelancers charge RM800–RM3,000 for one channel, boutique agencies RM3,000–RM8,000 for a managed mix, and ad spend is always budgeted separately on top.

If you've been quoted anywhere from RM500 to RM50,000 a month by different agencies and can't tell why the numbers are so far apart, you're not alone. This guide breaks down exactly what you get at each price point so you can budget realistically and spot a bad proposal before you sign.

## Digital Marketing Price in Malaysia at a Glance

| Scope | Typical monthly price |
| --- | --- |
| Entry / trial package | RM888 – RM1,500 |
| One channel, freelancer | RM800 – RM3,000 |
| Managed 2–3 channels, boutique agency | RM3,000 – RM8,000 |
| Full-service agency | RM8,000 – RM15,000 |
| Regional / enterprise | RM15,000 – RM50,000+ |

Ad spend is not included in any of these figures. It goes directly from your own account to Meta, TikTok or Google.

## Pricing by Provider Type

Who you hire has the biggest impact on price:

- **Freelancers**: RM800–RM3,000 a month, but usually covers only one channel (e.g. just social media, or just SEO). Good for very tight budgets, but you'll need to coordinate multiple freelancers yourself if you want a full strategy.
- **Boutique agencies**: RM3,000–RM8,000 a month for a managed mix of 2–3 channels with a dedicated account manager. This is the sweet spot for most established Malaysian SMEs.
- **Full-service agencies**: Starting around RM8,000 a month, covering strategy, content, paid ads, SEO, and reporting under one roof.
- **Major agencies**: RM15,000–RM50,000+ a month, typically serving larger brands or businesses expanding regionally across Southeast Asia.

If you're still deciding whether to hire out at all, it's worth reading our comparison of [in-house marketing vs hiring an agency](/blog/in-house-marketing-vs-agency-malaysia-sme-2026) before you start collecting quotes.

## What's Included at Each Price Point

A RM2,000/month package usually covers one channel — for example, 12–16 social media posts plus basic community management, with no paid ads or SEO included. A RM5,000/month package typically bundles social media management, basic SEO (on-page optimisation, monthly reporting), and light paid ads oversight. A RM10,000+/month package adds full SEO campaigns, multi-platform paid ads management, content production (video, photography), and dedicated strategy calls.

## Service-Specific Cost Benchmarks

If you're only budgeting for one channel, here's what Malaysian agencies typically charge:

- **Social media management**: RM1,200–RM2,000 a month for content creation and posting (excluding ad spend)
- **SEO**: Around RM1,500–RM4,000 a month for keyword research, on-page optimisation, and link building
- **Google/Meta Ads management**: RM800–RM2,500 a month in management fees, plus ad spend on top
- **Short-form video production**: RM800–RM2,000 per video, with per-video rates dropping when ordered in batches
- **Website design**: RM500–RM12,000 as a one-off project cost, not a monthly retainer

For a deeper look at whether the paid-ads line in that list earns its keep, see [is paid advertising worth it for Malaysian SMEs](/blog/is-paid-advertising-worth-it-malaysia-sme-2026).

## What Cheaper Nexus Actually Charges

Rather than leaving you with ranges, here is our own published price list — every figure is on our site, with no quote-on-request step:

- **First Trial Package — RM888**, one-time, once per company. One short video (filming, editing, script, copywriting), two professional designs, and Meta Ads foundation setup for one page. Original value RM3,100.
- **Social Media Management Package — RM2,888/month**. Two short videos, five professional designs plus IG feed, day-to-day management of one Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Xiaohongshu page each, and Meta ads management. Original value RM5,738.
- **Full Business Growth Package — RM8,888 / 3 months**. Six short videos, eighteen professional designs, full-channel management including Google Business Profile, Waze, Telegram and Lemon8, plus ads management. Original value RM10,888.
- **Standalone**: ads management from RM2,000/month, KOC/KOL influencer marketing from RM3,888 for 10 creators, professional design RM150 each (ten for RM800), and video RM800 each (ten for RM5,000).

None of these include ad spend or model and influencer talent fees. You can see [the actual work and the full price list on one page](/works#pricing) — real videos and designs delivered for Malaysian brands, sitting next to what each package costs.

## Retainer vs Project vs Percentage-of-Spend

Agencies in Malaysia typically bill in one of three ways:

1. **Monthly retainer** — a fixed fee regardless of results, most common for ongoing SEO, content, and social media work
2. **Project-based** — a one-off fee for a defined deliverable like a website build or a single campaign launch
3. **Percentage of ad spend** — usually 10%–20% of your monthly ad budget, common for paid advertising management

Ad spend itself is always separate from the agency fee. If an agency quotes RM3,000 a month and you set a RM5,000 ad budget, your real monthly outlay is RM8,000 — only RM5,000 goes toward actual ad clicks and impressions.

## Worked Example: What a RM4,500 Monthly Budget Buys

This is an illustration of how a budget splits, not a report of any client's results.

Take a Klang Valley restaurant with four outlets and RM4,500 a month to spend. A realistic split at that level would be roughly RM3,000 to a boutique agency for social content and Google Business Profile management, and RM1,500 as actual Meta ad spend. The agency fee buys the work; the RM1,500 buys the reach.

The point of writing it out this way is that **「RM4,500 a month」 on its own tells you nothing** — the same number can mean RM4,500 of service with no advertising at all, or RM1,000 of service with RM3,500 pushed into ads. Always ask for the split before comparing two quotes.

## Red Flags When Evaluating a Proposal

- **No clear breakdown between management fee and ad spend** — if a quote just says 「RM5,000/month, all-in」 with no split, ask for clarity before signing
- **Vague deliverables** like 「social media management」 with no post count, content calendar, or reporting cadence specified
- **Long lock-in contracts** (12+ months) with no exit clause for underperformance
- **Guaranteed rankings or guaranteed leads** — no legitimate agency can guarantee Google rankings or a fixed number of leads
- **No portfolio** — if an agency cannot show you work it has actually delivered, the price is irrelevant

## How to Choose the Right Budget for Your Business

1. Start with one or two channels that match where your customers actually search or scroll, rather than spreading a small budget across five channels
2. Ask for a breakdown of management fee vs ad spend vs one-off setup costs before comparing quotes
3. Request a 3-month minimum trial period rather than a 12-month lock-in, so you can evaluate results before committing further
4. Make sure you can measure what you're buying — our guide to [reading your Google Analytics 4 reports](/blog/google-analytics-4-malaysia-sme-guide-2026) covers the minimum setup for knowing whether the spend is working
5. Compare quotes against the benchmarks above — a quote far outside these ranges deserves a second look, in either direction

## Conclusion

Digital marketing prices in Malaysia vary widely because the packages themselves vary widely — a RM2,000 quote and a RM10,000 quote may both be reasonable, just for very different scopes of work. The useful question is never 「how much does digital marketing cost」 but 「how much of this number is service and how much is media」.

faq.q: What is the price of digital marketing in Malaysia?
faq.a: Digital marketing price in Malaysia runs from about RM888 for an entry package to RM15,000 a month for full-service work. Most SME retainers sit between RM1,500 and RM8,000 a month, with ad spend budgeted separately on top.

faq.q: How much does a digital marketing agency cost per month in Malaysia?
faq.a: Most Malaysian SME retainers run RM1,500–RM15,000 a month depending on scope: RM800–RM3,000 for freelancers, RM3,000–RM8,000 for boutique agencies, RM8,000+ for full-service agencies.

faq.q: Is ad spend included in the agency’s monthly fee?
faq.a: No. The agency fee covers strategy and management only. Ad spend on Google or Meta is budgeted separately and goes directly to the ad platform, not the agency.

faq.q: What is the cheapest way to start digital marketing in Malaysia?
faq.a: A one-off entry package is usually cheapest. Cheaper Nexus runs a RM888 First Trial Package (once per company) covering one short video, two designs and Meta Ads setup, so you can judge the quality before committing to a monthly retainer.

faq.q: What’s a reasonable price for social media management alone?
faq.a: Social media management alone typically costs RM1,200–RM2,000 a month in Malaysia for content and posting. A package that also includes video production and ads management, such as ours at RM2,888/month, sits above that range because the scope is wider.

faq.q: Should I hire a freelancer or an agency for digital marketing?
faq.a: Freelancers (RM800–RM3,000) work well for a single channel on a tight budget; agencies (RM3,000+) suit businesses needing 2 or more coordinated channels under one account manager and a portfolio you can check first.
